summary: The customer wants to design an initial laboratory comparison experiment and define what its results would demonstrate when using a spectral measurement interface combining MIR ATR and fluorescence to classify model biological tissues.

facts_stated.text: The research group is evaluating a spectral measurement interface on model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat, and liver.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: evaluating a spectral measurement interface using model biological tissues such as chicken muscle, fat and liver

facts_stated.text: The study is a laboratory classification study.
facts_stated.enquiry_quote: This is a laboratory classification study.

targets.purpose: laboratory classification of model biological tissues
compare spectral information from both modalities
targets.enquiry_quote: compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information

process.value: material is heterogeneous, causing sequential measurements to potentially sample different locations
process.enquiry_quote: the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location

customer_premises.claim: Sequential measurements will fail to sample the same location due to heterogeneity, justifying a combined interface.
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location

customer_premises.claim: MIR ATR and fluorescence can be directly compared or co-located without accounting for differing sampling depths (microns for ATR vs. millimeters for fluorescence).
customer_premises.enquiry_quote: compare MIR ATR and fluorescence information, because the material is heterogeneous and sequential measurements may not sample the same location

unknowns: Specific fluorophores targeted (autofluorescence vs. exogenous dyes) and relevant excitation/emission wavelength ranges
MIR spectral range of interest and ATR element material/geometry
Disparity in penetration depth between MIR ATR (evanescent wave, ~1–2 µm) and fluorescence (bulk/scattering, up to millimeters)
Interface geometry, spot size, and sample-probe contact pressure control
Sample preparation details (fresh, frozen/thawed, hydration maintenance, temperature)
Performance metrics and reference classification standards against which results will be evaluated
